rounds.text: Supra Pacific Financial Services Ltd is showing explosive fundamental momentum that has completely outpaced its modest share price appreciation [E38]. Compounded profit growth has surged by 111% over the last 5 years and accelerated to 212% over the last 3 years, backed by a 174% jump in trailing twelve-month profit growth [E19, E20, E21]. Despite this compounding power, the stock trades at an attractive P/E of 16.1x, which sits below its sector benchmark of 18.55x [E1, E6]. Valuation models indicate significant mispricing, with a discounted cash flow intrinsic value suggesting a margin of safety of 59.2%, and a reverse DCF showing the market price implies only 5.6% earnings growth against an 18.0% base case [E35, E36, E37]. Furthermore, insiders are backing this growth trajectory with real skin in the game, as promoter holding has increased significantly by 21.20 percentage points from Dec 2023 to reach 32.17% in Sep 2026 [E33]. Conceded: operating cash flow turned negative at Rs -66 Cr in Mar 2026 alongside a weak historical median return on equity of 5% [E25, E30].

Despite reported headline growth, Supra Pacific Financial Services Ltd suffers from an alarming collapse in cash generation, evidenced by an operating cash flow of Rs -66 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs -121 Cr in Mar 2026, dragging cash conversion down to -8.25x [E29, E30, E31]. This severe disconnect between accounting profits and actual cash reality is compounded by filed flags warning of a low interest coverage ratio and a suspicious tax rate [E43, E45]. Furthermore, historical return metrics reveal a mediocre core business, highlighted by a 10-year, 5-year, and 3-year median return on equity of just 5%, alongside filed warnings that promoter holding remains low at 32.2% [E25, E26, E27, E44]. Structural momentum is also showing cracks as current rules-based screens explicitly flag that earnings growth is decelerating [E52]. Conceded: the company has delivered strong historical sales and profit growth over 3, 5, and 10 years, and a discounted cash flow model suggests a wide margin of safety [E14, E15, E16, E18, E19, E20, E35, E36].

Conceded: operating cash flow and free cash flow were negative at Rs -66 Cr and Rs -121 Cr respectively in Mar 2026, leading to a cash conversion of -8.25x [E29, E30, E31]. However, the valuation more than compensates for cash volatility, with a discounted cash flow model showing an intrinsic value of Rs 83 against a market price of Rs 33.8, providing a substantial margin of safety of 59.2% [E35, E36]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that the current share price only demands an earnings growth expectation of 5.6%, which is easily overshadowed by the company's actual delivery of 174% profit growth in the trailing twelve months and 212% over 3 years [E20, E21, E37]. While median ROE over multiple periods stands at 5%, the latest metrics show significant improvement with an ROE of 8.38% outperforming the sector benchmark of 5.09%, and an ROCE of 10.28% beating the sector's 5.58% [E9, E10, E25, E26, E27]. The claim of low promoter holding ignores a substantial insider accumulation of +21.20 percentage points, bringing promoter stake up to 32.17% from 10.97% [E33]. Finally, concerns about decelerating growth are countered by fundamentals vastly outpacing share price movement, with 5-year profit growth at 111% compared to a mere 6% share price growth, supported by fresh positive triggers expecting a good quarter [E22, E38, E41, E52].

Conceded: promoter holding increased by 21.20 percentage points to reach 32.17% [E33]. However, the bull's reliance on a DCF intrinsic value of Rs 83 [E35] glosses over a severe structural flaw in earnings quality: operating cash flow collapsed to negative Rs -66 Cr and free cash flow dropped to negative Rs -121 Cr in March 2026, resulting in a disastrous cash conversion ratio of -8.25x [E29, E30, E31]. While the reverse DCF implies a low growth hurdle [E37], it ignores filed warnings that the company suffers from a low interest coverage ratio, an abnormally low tax rate, and decelerating earnings growth [E43, E45, E52]. The historical reality of the business cannot be erased by recent trailing spikes, given that the median return on equity has stagnated at a dismal 5% over 3, 5, and 10-year horizons [E25, E26, E27], alongside an official filing flag that promoter holding remains low at 32.2% [E44]. Finally, the claim of a significant margin of safety [E36] is undermined by rules-based scoring that places confidence at only medium with a score of 61 out of 100 [E47], rendering the bullish valuation models heavily vulnerable to cash burn.
